question: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE), Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE) Subject:

Increasingly often, European farmers are required to contribute to environmental and climate goals through practices that reduce emissions, protect soil, conserve water, preserve agricultural landscapes and support biodiversity. In many cases, however, the costs of adaptation are immediate, whereas the economic benefits for farms remain uncertain, insufficient, or difficult to access because of bureaucracy. For the ecological transition to be credible and accepted, farmers must be viewed not solely as targets of obligations, but also as suppliers of quantifiable public goods. In the absence of a clear, simple and predictable mechanism of payments for ecosystem services, there is a risk that green policies will be perceived as an additional burden rather than as an economic opportunity for rural areas. 1.

Does the Commission intend to propose a European legal framework for payments for ecosystem services provided by farmers, over and above the Carbon Farming Framework, based on measurable indicators and simplified procedures, so that the contribution made by agriculture to environmental and climate goals is recognised and fairly compensated?
What are the interim results of the actions announced in the Roadmap towards Nature Credits?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.8.2026) 1. The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) supports eco-schemes and environmental, climate-related and management commitments that contribute to the achievement of EU environmental and climate goals. Programmed and reported measurable indicators aim at monitoring the implementation of these interventions. Schemes can be based on achievements, to reward the results. The Commission proposal for future CAP includes incentive payments for agri-environmental-climate actions. Moving from compensation to incentives opens the way to reward environmental services. The Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming Regulation (CRCF)1 can support a results-based eco-scheme for farmers by establishing a voluntary EU certification framework by which farmers are rewarded for the carbon removed. The CRCF requires carbon farming activities to generate co-benefits for biodiversity, ecosystems, soil, water and climate adaptation. CRCF methodologies covering agriculture, agroforestry, rewetting of peatlands, and afforestation have been adopted on 9th July 2026. 2. The Commission adopted the Roadmap towards Nature Credits2. A dedicated Expert Group3 is advancing discussions on methodologies and metrics, governance and integrity, market readiness and finance, policy coherence, and international cooperation. Monitoring, reporting and verification will be developed under ongoing pilots that test the feasibility of a market for nature credits of nature positive actions for various ecosystems at EU scale.

1 Regulation (EU) 2024/3012 - https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:L_202403012. 2 https://green-forum.ec.europa.eu/green-business/nature-credits_en. 3 The Expert Group met in December 2025, March 2026 and 18 June 2026.
